I've farmed this land forty years. My father taught me, but I finished high school and I read the extension materials when they come. Let me think through this year carefully.

My main rotation is cabbage–maize–cabbage on 4 mu of my better land, with well irrigation. The other 2 mu I split: 1 mu for chili (gets good price at the county market), 0.5 mu for kidney bean (family eats most, some to sell), 0.5 mu for spinach in spring before it turns hot.

**Spring cabbage (4 mu):** I plant hybrid seed from the dealer in Quzhou town — I tried traditional once, heads were too loose, lost money. Last year I used 50 jin urea and 40 jin diammonium per mu, plus about 30 jin potassium sulfate. Cabbage is hungry for potassium or the heads crack. So about 20 kg N, 10 kg P, 15 kg K per mu. I irrigate 5 times — at transplant, head formation, and through heading. Spray 3 times for diamondback moth and aphids, that is the real problem here. I expect 4,500 kg per mu if weather cooperates.

**Summer maize (4 mu):** Hybrid Zhengdan or similar. After cabbage the soil still has nutrients, so I reduce — 14 kg N, 5 kg P, 5 kg K. Rainy season so only 2 irrigations if July is dry. One pesticide for borer. 580 kg per mu is what I usually get.

**Autumn cabbage (4 mu):** This is my money crop. Higher fertilizer — 22 kg N, 12 kg P, 18 kg K per mu. Six irrigations, four pesticide sprays. 5,200 kg per mu.

**Chili (1 mu):** Hybrid, needs heavy feeding. 20 kg N, 12 kg P, 18 kg K. Irrigate 9 times, spray 6 times — anthracnose and thrips are stubborn. 2,000 kg per mu fresh.

**Kidney bean (0.5 mu):** Improved variety, low N because it fixes its own. 6 kg N, 8 kg P, 10 kg K. 3 irrigations, 2 sprays. 180 kg per mu dry.

**Spinach (0.5 mu):** Improved, quick crop. 10 kg N, 5 kg P, 6 kg K, 3 irrigations, 1 spray. 1,500 kg per mu.

I plough the cabbage ground before spring planting; rotary till between cabbage and maize since time is tight.
